Repair & Overhaul Technician | Eindhoven Region Repair and overhaul Parts and machines with overhaul or repair work Working hours Language Dutch or English What will you be doing? This is repair and overhaul work. Parts and machines come in to you and go back out to specification, with the technical drawing as your reference. You disassemble them, assess what's worn or damaged, replace what needs replacing, and rebuild the whole as specified by the drawing. Overhaul work calls for a different kind of craftsmanship than building something new. You don't know in advance what you'll find, so your judgement determines what's needed. Anyone already doing this work in high-tech metalworking knows the difference. Repairing parts and machines according to technical drawings; Disassembling and assessing incoming parts; Carrying out overhaul work and replacing worn or damaged parts; Rebuilding and checking that everything is back to specification; Recording your findings and the work carried out. What do we offer? Gross monthly salary between €2,700 and €3,200 Room to grow in your trade Appreciation for your dedication, character, and craftsmanship An environment where collaboration, respect, and a down-to-earth attitude come first What you bring You've got overhaul and repair work in your hands: you can see what's happened to a part and know what it takes to bring it back to specification. You read a drawing without hesitation. Experience with overhaul or repair work; Reading technical drawings; Dutch or English. About the company You'll work at a company in high-tech metalworking that supplies solutions to clients in the Netherlands and abroad. Collaboration, respect, and a down-to-earth attitude are central, and you'll have the room to be yourself and show what you're good at. As a maintenance mechanic, you will work in a large, fully automated distribution centre where technology is constantly in motion. Conveyor systems, roller conveyors, lifts and other automated installations ensure that enormous volumes of goods are moved throughout the warehouse. If a system comes to a standstill, that is where your work becomes interesting: identifying the cause of the problem and getting the system back up and running as quickly as possible.You will work with a broad combination of mechanical engineering, electrical engineering and control technology. One fault may be caused by a mechanical component, while the next may require electrical troubleshooting or analysing the control system. You will look beyond simply replacing a faulty component: you will determine the root cause and identify what is needed to resolve the issue properly.Using advanced monitoring applications, you can see what is happening within the system and systematically identify technical and system-related faults. You will carry out repairs and maintenance and accurately document significant breakdowns and maintenance activities.It is precisely this combination that makes the role so interesting: rather than working on a single machine, you will work with an entire automated system in which different technologies come together.
